- doc. a5-0382/2000 by mrs de veyrac, on behalf of the committee on culture, youth, education, the media and sport, on the application of the convention on the protection of the world cultural and natural heritage in the states of the european union (com (2000) 2036 final)
the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to thank mrs van der laan for her report. the commission welcomes your report. in most of the areas which were the focus of the 1997 discharge procedure, you have stated that the commission's actions are to be welcomed because we are on the right track. i am therefore pleased that parliament is praising the commission at the beginning of the year. i do not want to stop there, but i would like to address the areas where you continue to criticise and call for further action, namely in the field of human resources and external aid. in the area of human resources, your report deals in particular with the question of the legal basis for the early retirement scheme. i would like to remind you that the commission adopted a proposal before christmas, which is now undergoing the interinstitutional consultation procedure and will be sent to parliament in february. the key data are: the commission is proposing to introduce an early retirement scheme for 600 people. however, due to budgetary neutrality, only 248 new recruits are to be made. who is eligible for the scheme? the official must be at least 50 years old and have completed at least 10 years' service. the scheme also provides for the payment of an early retirement pension of 60 to 70% of the salary, depending on age and length of service. the measure is voluntary. there is no legal entitlement either, but the commission will choose, on the basis of objective criteria, who can benefit from the early retirement scheme, in order to ensure, through this selection procedure, that the objective of a general increase in efficiency in the personnel field is actually achieved. the second point in the personnel policy concerns disciplinary procedures. in its january report, parliament proposed an external budgetary discipline chamber within the ecj or the european court of auditors. you have mentioned this proposal again today. i should like to summarize again the reasons which my colleague, neil kinnock, has set out in great detail for the commission's refusal to accept this proposal. the european treaties give the court of auditors and the european court of justice specific tasks: the court of auditors is responsible for the external control of the finances, and the ecj has the function of monitoring, where appropriate, the disciplinary procedures carried out by the commission. the commission considers that the involvement of the courts directly in the commission's internal procedures would give rise to conflicts of interest. the commission would also point out that in all international organisations the institutions themselves are responsible for the discipline of their staff. the commission firmly believes that the same should apply to the european commission. of course, action is needed. that was objectively obvious. before the end of the year we adopted the proposals mentioned by mr bösch, which are now in the consultation procedure. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the rules on the protection of the environment are respected, and i would like to ask the commissioner to take this opportunity to explain why the commission has not taken this step. the first steps are to establish an investigation and disciplinary office in the directorate-general for personnel and administration. i would like to inform you that it is always asked whether olaf is already involved in the procedure or intends to be involved in the procedure before this office is involved. only if olaf rejects this will the office take action. the situations can be very different. let me give you an example: sexual harassment in the workplace. since olaf may not act in such a case, an administrative inquiry or disciplinary action is of course necessary. so there are different areas to think about. i think it's very good to be complementary. it is not a question of taking away olaf's tasks or undermining olaf's remit as defined by parliament and the council, but rather of giving priority to olaf's investigation. secondly, it is very important that the disciplinary board be chaired by an external expert. this demonstrates the commission's commitment to fair and objective disciplinary proceedings. i would like to say a few words about your criticisms of foreign policy. mrs theato mentioned the reduction of outstanding commitments. we have submitted a report on this subject in the 2001 budgetary procedure, and we have made it clear that, of course, it is particularly important to reduce these abnormal outstanding commitments, which have been in abeyance for a long time and which need to be dismantled as quickly as possible. the hospital in the gaza strip, which plays a major role in mrs van der laan's report, is now being examined. in fact, there have been a lot of annoying delays. parliament has repeatedly insisted that this should be done and that all the problems should be tackled. yes, it is very gratifying that the hospital is now fully operational and has been treating patients since the summer. but political developments, violent conflicts, have again created barriers. in fact, some of the blockades in gaza prevent the delivery of equipment and the access of patients. a lot of the staff can't get into the hospital right now. it is really necessary to call again and again, also in this debate, for an end to the violence. the european taxpayer was prepared to provide aid to the people of the gaza strip. now, at last, the people should be able to use this aid.
, deputy rapporteur - mr president, i should like to begin by praising the good work of my colleague, mr salvador garriga polledo, in his report on own resources, a subject which he has been following very closely for some time. the community budget is partly financed by the traditional own resources of the customs services of the member states and the main role of the community's regulatory system of guarantees and suretyships is therefore to protect the community's financial interest. the failures in the procedures applicable to the system of guarantees and guarantees mean exactly that the corresponding community revenue is not collected, which has to be covered by additional contributions from the gross national product of the member states. i therefore believe that interest should be charged to traders who actually use unauthorised credit for their deferred payments in the context of free circulation operations. the garriga polledo report deals with cases of liability of member states where non-application of community rules on guarantees and sureties causes damage to the community interest. the court of auditors reminds us that, in the case of mandatory guarantees, the basic principle is that the customs authorities set the guarantee at a level equivalent to the exact amount of the customs debt where this can be established with certainty, and if not, the maximum amount as calculated by the customs authorities of the customs debts that have been or may be incurred. in practice, it is the guarantee body which assesses the risks of the operation. for the assessment of those risks, the guarantee should be set at a level as close as possible to the customs debt for which the guarantee was granted. if these rules were to be observed, the relevant financial interests would be fully protected. there are difficulties which we are facing and of which i will highlight half a dozen: firstly, there are no reliable statistics on the volume of guarantees currently agreed. the data relating to these guarantees and guarantees - clearly identified from an accounting or legal point of view - exist in the customs accounting services of the member states, but there are no measures to enable them to be compared and known at community level. secondly, some customs authorities are not able - i prefer to accept that hypothesis rather than think that they are not cooperating - to monitor effectively compliance with the requirements laid down in community legislation on guarantees because of imperfections in their operating systems and procedures or accounting. i have to point out the need for the new transit computing system (nsit) to be put into effect soon in all member states and countries associated with the common transit system. it is clear that the fulfilment of the community commitments will depend to a large extent on the development of all the nsit's functionalities. in order to solve the problem of the large number of unpaid transit operations, we should stress the importance of operational measures and, once again, the need for a rapid development of this new system. the multiple guarantee certification system and the nsit will bring about centralization and greater administrative clarity. thirdly, we must point out the incomplete declarations. at the end of the periods allowed under community rules, member states should transfer to the 'a' accounting the rights covered by a guarantee which are not subject to challenge. fourthly, the need for an amendment to community customs legislation to ensure that the guarantors who guarantee the right of credit also guarantee the ex officio clearance of goods issued by the customs services after the release of goods. fifthly, the large number of cases reported by the court of auditors in which amounts due to the community budget have not been paid or are received with the relevant interest late. finally, i would like to mention the difficulties which result in the failure to collect the considerable amounts of customs duties and other taxes which arise from tir operations, and which are attributable to the ineffective implementation of the existing mechanisms and the lack of supervision in transit. in conclusion, mr president, i would like to stress that the european commission must study the various problems raised and, in particular, must revise the computer system so that it takes account of the interests owed in this respect to the community budget by the member states.

- mr president, the parish report rigorously analyses a question which is essential for community europe and for anyone who aspires to join the union. young farmers require priority attention. firstly, because we must support our young people in all sectors of activity, and secondly, because we are interested in the territorial fixation of the rural population, most of whom are involved in of farmers. and even among the latter, i would distinguish between those who are the sons of farmers who work the land and the descendants of farmers who, because of the size of their property, are the commission is aware of the fact that the united states has been involved in the negotiations for the establishment of the international criminal court, and that the united states has been involved in the negotiations for the establishment of the international criminal court. at european level, a non-binding common position of 4 march 1996, also adopted under the maastricht treaty, on the european asylum system in the medium term. the commission intends to present concrete proposals in 2001 for both these areas. and these concrete proposals will take account of the specific situations of women who are victims of abuse and ill-treatment. the commission has already begun to develop some measures to address the specific situation of these women. this is the case, for example, with the proposal for a directive on temporary protection in the event of a mass influx of displaced persons, which we presented on 24 may last year. in this proposal, under article 11 (4), member states are obliged to provide appropriate medical assistance or other forms of assistance to women who are victims of torture, rape or other serious forms of psychological, physical or sexual violence. similarly, in the commission's proposal on minimum standards for the procedure for granting and withdrawing refugee status, which the commission adopted on 20 september 2000, there are several rules which concern the specific needs of women, for example article 4 (4), which provides that women may submit an asylum application separately from their husbands, article 3 (8), which enshrines the principle of the independent and separate interview of women in relation to the asylum application, article 8 (7), which gives women the right to change interviewer and interpreter if they feel that they are inhibited from stating the reasons for their asylum application by the fact that the interviewer or interpreter is of the male sex, in particular in situations of sexual abuse, and finally article 14 (1) (c), which provides for an obligation on member states to ensure that vulnerable women in such situations are provided with the basic interview staff needed to deal with the specific problems of such training. the commission also intends to introduce provisions on people with special needs in its proposal for a directive on reception conditions for asylum seekers, which will be presented in the first quarter of this year. as regards the specific question of whether persecution on grounds of sex should be a basis for asylum, the commission has already launched a wide-ranging consultation on this subject and we hope that the necessary conclusions will be drawn during the course of this year in order to submit to parliament and the council a proposal for subsidiary protection which may also cover such situations.
- thank you very much, mr vitorino, because i understand that the commission intends to put forward proposals. i would like to say that in the last decade of the century that has ended, both the vienna conference and subsequently the beijing conference opened up new horizons for us to take account of the very specific situation that women suffer in many countries, but i think the commissioner understands what mrs izquierdo has raised, and i am grateful that she is going to make these kinds of proposals.

- question no 30 by mr jonas sjöstedt (h-0972/00): subject: export of mining waste during the 1980s, the swedish mining company boliden exported a large quantity of toxic waste to arica, chile, for recycling. however, as the waste was stored in an open landfill, heavy metals were released into the environment, causing serious health problems for the local population. chile then demanded that the remaining waste be shipped back to sweden. does the commission consider that the export referred to above was carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions? does it also consider that the boliden company now has a part of the responsibility for remedying the situation?
the commission. the transport of waste, including transport to and from the community, is regulated by regulation 259/93. this regulation replaced directive 84/631 on the transboundary movement of hazardous waste. this revision incorporates the provisions of the 1989 basel convention on the transport of hazardous waste into community law. from 1 january 1998, the community has therefore prohibited all shipments of hazardous waste to be used for recycling or to be deposited in non-oecd countries. the community therefore follows the 1995 amendment to the basel convention which has not yet entered into force internationally. however, this legislation does not apply to exports of waste from the swedish mining company boliden to chile in the 1980s because sweden was not a member of the eu at that time. moreover, the basel convention provisions were not applicable in the 1980s. in this particular case, the commission considers that there is no community legislation which can now make the company liable for any environmental impact of these waste products. the question of bolidens' liability in this case therefore becomes a national issue which must be resolved through national environmental legislation.
the answer to that question is yes. there is currently a ban on the export of hazardous waste, including to third countries, i.e. outside the eu.

- question no 42 by mrs concepció ferrer (h-0981/00) subject: situation of burundian refugees in tanzania according to information received from the lukole (ngara) camp, the food situation in the burundian refugee camps does not seem to have improved and there are even indications that preparations are being made for the repatriation of burundian refugees currently in tanzania. in view of the resolution adopted by the acp-eu parliamentary assembly (acp-eu 3005/00/def.), and in particular paragraph 15 thereof, in which it is requested that 'the commission, the council and the representatives of the member states in international organizations take appropriate measures as a matter of urgency to deal with the situation in the refugee camps of hutus from burundi in tanzania', and considering that several months have elapsed since the adoption of that resolution, could the commission state what measures it has taken to implement that paragraph of acp-eu 3005/00/def.?
commission. – i am pleased to inform the honourable member and this house that the commission has taken and continues to take appropriate measures in relation to the nutrition and repatriation situation of burundian refugees in tanzania. i visited tanzania in march 2000 and on that occasion i also went to see camps with refugees from burundi. the overall number of refugees in tanzania, including those from burundi, continues to grow. by the end of 2000 there were approximately 500 000 refugees in camps in western tanzania of whom around 360 000 were burundians, 110 000 congolese and the remainder rwandans, somalis and other nationalities. through echo the commission funds more than one third of the total humanitarian aid available to refugees in tanzania. in the year 2000, echo's budget for aid to tanzanian refugees was eur 26.85 m. echo's level of support is expected to remain substantially the same this year. the key partners in tanzania are the international federation of the red cross and red crescent, the unhcr, unicef and the world food programme. the main objectives of the humanitarian aid are multi-sector care of refugees, feeding, education, health care for children and finally, public health, water and sanitation in the camps. as to the standard of nutrition inside the camps, echo contributes one third of the total cost of the world food programme in tanzania, which provides a balanced daily ration of 2166 calories per refugee, well over the minimum recommended by the who. the wfp recently alerted the international community to potential problems of supply, which would be due to delays in funding from sources other than the commission, and daily rations were temporarily reduced to 80%. however, the rations remained adequate in view of the fact that many refugees have access to additional sources of food. in 1999, fao joined the international relief operation by introducing a programme to improve nutrition standards among the most vulnerable households. in collaboration with unhcr, fao provided 15 000 families in six of the camps with seeds and hand tools in order to plant household and community vegetable gardens. training was given and fao estimates that more than 50 000 people have benefited directly from the project. i have seen this programme and it is in fact so well-organised and so neat that the alternative that we can offer the refugees when they return looks much less organised. but, of course, this is what we are going to support. concerning the possible repatriation of burundian refugees in tanzania following the signing of the peace agreement at the arusha summit, the commission is maintaining a state of readiness for this eventuality. i was myself present at the burundi donors' conference chaired by nelson mandela in paris in december, which endorsed the peace agreement. the commission is pursuing a twin-track approach. firstly, the current level of humanitarian assistance to refugees will be maintained while they remain in tanzania. secondly, should the conditions be met for their repatriation – and we are pushing everybody concerned and some who do not think they should be concerned to make this happen – then the funds allocated by echo to the tanzania programme will follow the refugees back home. an additional sum of eur 25 million has been allocated by the development dg under the lomé convention's article 255 to assist unhcr in a planned and orderly repatriation. at this stage, the preconditions for an orderly and voluntary repatriation unfortunately are not met. this was discussed in echo's annual strategic programming meeting with unhcr in december when it was agreed that repatriation may only take place if all parties are convinced that the security situation inside burundi is stabilised and sustainable. this is a major operation of ours and we want to follow it through to a successful conclusion.
- commissioner, i think it is only fair to thank you for such a comprehensive answer which gives me some measure of peace of mind. i think that the same is true of you, because there is no doubt that the problems of these numerous refugees in tanzania are serious. we had the world food programme report telling us that by the end of the year, the food reserves would be exhausted. there is also the need to allow training and education for all these refugees, even if they are in an anomalous situation in their lives, precisely so that these years are not wasted years. it is therefore essential not only to provide humanitarian aid in the form of food, but also to have educational and health programmes so that these tragic years for the burundian people are not wasted years but can be the breeding ground for a better era and, above all, for a definitive reconciliation of the burundian people.

the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have to say that i am very pleased with the way the commission has been working. i am happy to make the requested statement on the union's fisheries relations with morocco at the outset. you may have heard from the media that negotiations with the kingdom of morocco on a new form of cooperation in the fisheries sector began after i went to casablanca in october and agreed with the king of morocco that serious negotiations would be started. the commission has also decided to extend the period of validity of the aid to the following areas: in early january i met twice - once for three days, once for two days - to discuss with prime minister youssoufi and minister chbaatou. i have made a great effort to create understanding on both sides as regards the main aspects of future fisheries relations, and in particular as regards fishing opportunities, the duration of the contract, the technical conditions for fishing and, in particular, the financial compensation. between the first and second political meetings this year, negotiations took place almost every day, most recently at technical level. the work was carried on in a very constructive manner and many details were clarified. the commission has tried throughout the negotiations to be as flexible as possible in the most important moroccan demands as we see fit, particularly as regards the level of fishing opportunities and the compulsory landings in moroccan ports. we have always stated from the outset that we are ready to take account of moroccan interests and to support the development of the moroccan fisheries sector. we have always been clear that we want to protect the social and economic interests of the community and that we want to cooperate in the conservation of resources. unfortunately, on my second visit on 8 and 9 january, the moroccan side suddenly took a very rigid stance, particularly on the important issues of fishing opportunities and technical conditions, and made extremely high demands for financial compensation. i have therefore asked the moroccan side to reconsider its position, since no agreement is possible on this basis, and i have asked for talks to resume as soon as possible with a view to reaching a final conclusion. we are prepared to pay a fair price for a balanced agreement, but it must be proportionate to the fishing opportunities granted by morocco. i have always made this clear to the moroccan side. if our moroccan partners return to the negotiating table and show a willingness to negotiate, i am sure that we will eventually reach a mutually acceptable solution. in conclusion, i would like to point out that cooperation with morocco in the fisheries sector was also a central point of president prodi's visit to morocco, and on this occasion too both sides reaffirmed their intention to conclude an agreement. it was also agreed that we should resume negotiations at technical level as soon as possible.

the rapporteur. - mr. president, thank you very much for your understanding. i would like to thank commissioner fischler for his statement on the fisheries agreement with morocco and i would also like to thank him for all the efforts he is making in this difficult negotiation. we all knew it was going to be difficult and long. and i want to recall here, as he has said, but i want to emphasize it, that this is the first time that a president of the european commission has been personally involved in a negotiation of a fisheries agreement. it must be clear to the citizens of the european union and to morocco that all the institutions of the european union, and at the highest level, want this agreement: the european council wants it, as it said in nice, the president of the commission wants it, as he said in rabat, and the european parliament wants it in strasbourg. so for the moment, morocco is the one that does not want it, at least under the logical conditions demanded by the european union. we hope that we will be able to convince him of the mutual benefits of this agreement and that we can thus associate president prodi with its success. i simply ask you, mr fischler, to resume the negotiations as soon as possible - immediately, if possible - taking advantage of the impetus given by the president of the european commission himself. and i do not want morocco, as has been said here too, to distract us from the very important debate we are having here today. we have been called to discuss four important reports which have to do with the common fisheries policy and its future. i shall naturally concentrate on my own, for which i am the rapporteur, but i would like to congratulate mr poignant and mr gallagher, and also mr cunha, on the excellent work they have done. i would also like to point out that the report i am presenting is the first that a community institution has produced on the subject of globalisation in fisheries, and i therefore believe that our committee has been right in the two own-initiative reports it has decided to produce; the other is still in progress. the first point i want to make in this report is that, commissioner, fishing in the european union must begin to lose the almost domestic or marginal status it currently enjoys, perhaps because of its confinement to peripheral regions or because of the coldness of the figures, which are always talked about, for the contribution of the community's gdp. the global dimension of fisheries must be recognized. we are increasingly dependent on fish imports; we have our own fleet on all the seas and we have sufficient technical know-how of our own not to leave this strategic sector in the hands of third countries. the 2002 reform must not therefore be used merely to continue to look at the navel of our own community waters, our own problems and our own miseries. we definitely need a fleet that is well-sized and competitive, both at european and world level. and more competitive does not mean more predatory, but simply more efficient in exploiting the resources actually available, and doing it better than others. fisheries is, and will increasingly be, a strategic sector as a food reserve: healthy and safe animal protein for a growing humanity. we must involve fisheries - and this is also the result of the fisheries agreement with morocco - in the european union's foreign and trade policy. the union's external fisheries policy must gain credibility and an image which it does not yet have, by standing up to world public opinion as what it really is: the policy of a fishing power which is consistent with the principles of the united nations, that is, the development of the international law of the sea, the conservation of everyone's resources, development cooperation, etc. let us therefore pursue an active policy, both in the fisheries agreements with third countries, adapted to each situation, and in the regional fisheries organisations, which we must lead, as we have said many times, and not be satisfied with the fact that the 15 states which today make up the european union - tomorrow, perhaps 20 or 25 - must always have the same weight as estonia today, for example. the council of ministers of the european union or the united nations security council are examples of votes weighted by the specific weight of territories and populations, and we must take this important example into account. our report says that the european union has not yet become aware of the importance of its fisheries interests at international level. it is true, as we said earlier, that the relative weight in community gdp is small, but we must not forget that we are the fourth largest fleet in the world. and if we add to this fleet the processing industry, the marketing industry, the auxiliary industries, investments in other countries and specialized shipbuilding, we are without a doubt faced with the world's largest conglomerate of economic activity linked to fisheries. other powers, such as the united states and japan, are aware of this and are investing in this sector. in the wto we have to defend our interests without any qualms. and our structural aid system too, since not all of it relates to fisheries, some of it is aid to conserve and control resources, to provide more safety for vessels, to improve fishing infrastructure and selective fishing gear. in the wto we must demand real liberalisation of port services, freedom of investment and establishment in third countries with full legal guarantees and freedom of access to ports. we must denounce the attempts to extend the exclusive economic zones and lead the effective fight against flags of convenience. all this, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, is the real challenge for the common fisheries policy in the face of the globalisation of the economy. the european parliament is today presenting this report, to which i refer, as a reflection for all of us on the eve of a historic reform of the common fisheries policy, so that we can all be clear about where we are and where we need to go.

the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have to say that i am very pleased with the way the commission has been working. i would like to begin by thanking all the rapporteurs, the committee on fisheries and the other committees involved, on behalf of the commission, for the extensive work they have done in preparing this debate. i would also like to thank the chairman of the committee on fisheries, mr varela, for coordinating all the work and for his interesting own-initiative report. mr varela, you make it very clear in this report that we cannot talk about the future of the common fisheries policy without taking into account the wider economic environment of fishing. like any other economic activity, fisheries is affected by globalisation. i can fully endorse many of the points in your report and the resolution that accompanies it. they stress that the european fisheries policy is committed to the principle of multi-functionality, i.e. a sustainable fisheries economy that preserves fishery resources and protects the marine environment, and in which coastal fishing regions make an important contribution to economic and social structures. i would also like to thank you in particular for your support in the fight against illegal and irresponsible fishing. we shall have occasion to discuss community solutions to this burning problem. i am convinced that you too would like to see a more decisive approach. i think there are three points in the report which need to be discussed. firstly, i note in the report a certain tendency towards greater protection against international competition. the reason for this is that fisheries are an important employer in certain coastal regions. that is certainly true, but if we insist unilaterally that jobs must be maintained by means of fisheries policy alone, and do not take into account the local situation of a coastal region as a whole, we run the risk of subsidizing in the wrong direction. that would be counterproductive both for fisheries resources and for jobs. the fisheries sector must be able to stand on its own two feet. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. perhaps the most effective way of helping is to give a future to young people in particular and to offer them alternative employment opportunities to fishing. secondly, i would like to refer to the wto negotiations you mentioned. as you know, at present there is no agreement on whether or not a new round of wto negotiations will be launched and what its scope will be. but even if there is a full round, i doubt that the community would be prepared to be reciprocal in fisheries on the issues that will be discussed, such as investment or the right of establishment. in most member states, only nationals of eu countries or eu citizens are allowed to invest in the fisheries sector. thirdly, i would remind you that from the very beginning of the common fisheries policy it has been accepted that the community has one seat and one voice. the purely numerical disadvantage is largely offset by the advantage of greater influence in shaping international fisheries policy. in conclusion, mr varela, i would like to say that your report has made an important contribution to the further discussion on the future of the common fisheries policy. the commission will certainly take account of its considerations in its forthcoming green paper as far as possible. i come now to the reports and motions for resolutions by mr gallagher and mr poignant. the two reports share a common starting point. the community's fishing industry is under pressure from several sides. fish stocks are declining, the fleet is overcapacitated and access to third country waters is becoming increasingly difficult. i am glad that you essentially agree with the analysis of the commission's report on the application of the fisheries policy for the period 1996-98. while some progress has been made - i would just like to mention the flexibility in annual stock management, or the new tacs for non-regulated north sea species, or the regulation on technical measures, or the introduction of the vms - we must admit that we have not been able to reverse the negative trends in many of the commercially important stocks, such as cod or hake. the two rapporteurs also highlight the following serious shortcomings, which have already been identified in the commission report: the limitations on fishing effort have not worked or have not worked sufficiently, the regulation on technical measures in the mediterranean has been implemented only incompletely, the map 4 is far from ambitious enough, the control provisions have not been strengthened as we proposed in 1998. the meetings with the various representatives of the fisheries sector also showed that we need to improve or even completely revamp many aspects of fisheries policy in order to achieve responsible, sustainable fishing. despite the diversity of opinions, the majority of those concerned agree that we need to do more. in particular, we must strengthen controls, better implement the rules, reduce discards, promote scientific research and involve the parties concerned, in particular the fishermen themselves, earlier and more intensively in the decision-making process on fisheries policy. the commission therefore agrees with the two motions for resolutions on many points. however, on the sensitive issue of the six or twelve-mile zone, the commission has the impression that a majority of those concerned are in favour of maintaining the status quo. in a few weeks' time the commission will publish the green paper together with the reports referred to in article 14 (2) of regulation 3760. we must use the discussion which will then begin to discuss how to remedy the shortcomings identified in the reports and what appropriate solutions - the agenda calls for question time with the council (b5-0001/2001). i call question no 1 by mrs maj britt theorin (h-0952/00): subject: eu-china summit a recent iom report shows that the chinese trafficking mafia is extremely well organized and that the trade is carried out throughout china. at the same time, as incomes are relatively high (often over eur 30 000), the iom fears a very high increase in the trafficking of chinese women, both domestically and to western europe in particular. at the eu-china summit on 23 october 2000, the european council and the commission addressed the issue of responsibility for the repatriation of illegal chinese immigrants. has the council also addressed the problem of the vast trade in chinese women and girls?
the council. the council welcomed the opening of a dialogue with china on migration issues, in particular those relating to illegal migration and the return of chinese nationals found illegally staying in the territory of the member states. a meeting was held in brussels with officials from the presidency, the commission and a chinese delegation to identify and define areas of possible future cooperation. in particular, the exchange of information between authorities and organisations dealing with issues relating to trafficking in human beings and illegal migration was emphasised. more such meetings are planned, with the next to be held in beijing in a few weeks' time. preparations for that meeting are currently under way at expert level. as mr theorin will be aware, the european council in santa maria da feira expressed its concern at the tragic events in dover last year and condemned the criminal acts committed by those who profit from such human smuggling. the european council instructed the union to step up cooperation in combating such crossborder crime. the french presidency responded to the european council's call and put forward a number of initiatives to combat the criminal networks involved in the smuggling and trafficking of human beings. although the specific problem mentioned by theorin was not discussed at the eu-china meeting on 23 october last year, the council is very aware of the problem of trafficking in women and girls. this is not just trade from china but also from certain other countries not far from the eu. as chairman of asem, in which china is also involved, sweden raised the issue of trafficking in women and children in autumn 2000. the first step was a meeting of experts at the end of november last year, attended by experts in the field from both asia and europe. the recommendations of this meeting will be presented at the asem foreign ministers' meeting in beijing in may this year.
there is every reason for the working groups now set up to make rapid and effective contacts within the union's work with other international organisations dealing with these issues. the iom is probably the organisation with the most knowledge in this field. i assume that such contacts will be established very quickly. let me also stress that the fight against trafficking in women is generally highlighted as an important issue in the swedish presidency's work programme. we want to work against this terrible phenomenon on a broad front, not just in china but also globally.
- question no 2 is therefore inadmissible. i call question no 3 by mr david robert bowe (h-0956/00): subject: services provided to citizens of the european union in mecca in accordance with article 20 of the ec treaty, any citizen of the union enjoys the protection of the diplomatic and consular authorities of any member state in the territory of a third country where the member state of which he is a national is not represented, may the council therefore indicate what services are provided by the european union to citizens of the european union in mecca during the pilgrimage?
i cannot simply assure the honourable member that the matter will be taken up. i might even reassure him that his concern is somewhat unwarranted. the decision to which i referred earlier provides that if the person seeking consular assistance is a national of one of the member states of the union, the diplomatic or consular representation of another member state shall treat the applicant as if he were a national of the member state represented by the embassy or consulate. so the discriminatory situation that the honourable member fears should not arise, but a citizen of the union should be treated equally. i am convinced that the uk representation in this case stands in solidarity and treats all union citizens equally. this is at least stated in the decisions taken.
- question no 4 by mr paul rübig (h-0957/00) subject: market surveillance in the field of labelling
the council. the council is keen to have effective market surveillance in order to ensure that the basic requirements of the directives on ce marking, which have been drawn up on the basis of the so-called new method, are met. this method is a new way of harmonizing technical requirements for goods in directives. the monitoring of the use of this ce marking on products is a matter of common concern to the commission and the member states. it is primarily the responsibility of the member states to ensure, by means of accreditation or otherwise, that those bodies meet the requirements for competence and function effectively. the commission has been given a key role in ensuring consistency and high standards in the supervisory bodies. the supervisory bodies are national and the member states notify the commission of the national bodies responsible for carrying out the controls. the commission, in turn, establishes programmes to ensure that market surveillance is organised in a uniform manner across the member states. to monitor the new methodology, the bodies notified by the member states set up, for example, working groups for each directive.
as i mentioned earlier in my introductory reply to the honourable member, it is primarily the commission's responsibility to ensure uniformity in the assessment of so-called conformity. i would therefore suggest that the honourable member first of all turn to the commission for any further information on this matter.
- question no 5 by mr alexandros alavanos (h-0965/00) subject: hunger strike of political prisoners in turkey in turkey, a fatal outcome awaits dozens of political prisoners who have been on hunger strike for almost two months and who intend to carry it out to the end in protest against inhumane conditions of detention. at the same time, the council of europe states that torture remains a common practice in turkish police stations. amnesty international condemns torture, but also the impunity enjoyed by the perpetrators and, in general, all human rights violations in the country; the european union must demand an immediate end to torture, not later than 2002 or 2003, as provided for in the accession procedure. will the council intervene with the turkish authorities to obtain improvements in the prison system and thus bring the hunger strike to an end? will it accede to amnesty international's request for an immediate end to torture in the context of the accession procedure?
let me just remind you that the draft partnership agreement with turkey, which the council now considers to be in existence, offers an excellent opportunity to keep a constant 'eye on' turkey in the field of torture, prison conditions and human rights in general. the council will of course use all the possibilities available under this agreement to ensure that developments in turkey take a direction consistent with the common values we share in the union.
in fact, i can answer sjöstedt's question in the same way as i answered the previous question. the union's declaration of turkey as a candidate for membership, which was made at the helsinki summit, gives us a completely different opportunity to monitor developments in turkey closely and to point out any deviation from the standards that should apply to a candidate country. i therefore see it as a very urgent task, also under the swedish presidency, to ensure that developments in turkey take a path which will eventually allow us to see the country approach the european family in a more concrete way than hitherto.
- question no 6 by mr jonas sjöstedt (h-0967/00): subject: open meetings of the council the swedish presidency stressed the crucial importance of transparency in the european union's activities. how many fully public meetings will the council hold during the swedish presidency, from 1 january to 30 june 2001?
the council. as the presentation of the work programme by the prime minister a short while ago certainly showed, the swedish presidency attaches particular importance to the fact that the work of the council is public and accessible to european citizens and that legislative work is transparent. the swedish presidency is actively working to ensure that as many debates as possible are open, within the formal framework. the council's rules of procedure do not allow for fully public council meetings, as mr sjöstedt is well aware. however, public council debates may be held. at the helsinki european council in december 1999, the general affairs council and the ecofin council decided to hold public debates on the council's work programme every six months. this decision has now been incorporated into the council's rules of procedure. other council configurations also hold public debates. one of the first priorities of the swedish presidency was therefore to establish a list of public debates to cover as much of the council's work as possible. we have therefore now presented a list of the public debates to be held under our presidency. nine such debates will be held in what can be regarded as the important and central council configurations, starting as early as friday when ecofin is holding a debate on its work programme. the debate then progresses over the six months to the final open debate in the council (culture) in june on the protection of minors from harmful content in the media. we have thus taken these measures a step further towards greater openness in the council's work. there are certainly further steps to be taken, but don't let the best be the enemy of the good, mr sjöstedt!
as sjöstedt is well aware, the swedish presidency intends to use all possible energy to try to move forward on the transparency issue during the swedish presidency. we think we are doing so by increasing the number of debates that are open. we can draw parallels with most national parliaments. take the swedish parliament, for example. the legislative work of the committees of the swedish parliament is not public but it is closed, and there are reasons for this. there is a need for political consensus, but there is also, of course, a need for maximum transparency. i can assure you, sjöstedt, that we will do everything to move the positions forward but rome was not built in a day. even a long march begins with a small step.
- question no 7 by mr lennart sacrédeus (h-0970/00) subject: democracy and human rights in belarus on the basis of its common values, the eu considers it its duty to defend democracy, human rights and the rule of law. latvia, lithuania and poland, which are candidate countries, are neighbours of belarus, where none of the three principles mentioned above can be said to be respected in an acceptable manner, with the obvious risks of spread to neighbouring states that arise from this. the parliamentary troika of the eu, the council of europe and the osce presented a critical report on the violations of democracy in belarus in connection with the recent elections in minsk on 16 october. among the many people who have disappeared are former interior minister yuri zaherenko, former deputy speaker of parliament victor gonchar and russian filmmaker dmitri zavadski. what concrete initiatives does the swedish presidency intend to take to help improve the situation in belarus from the point of view of democracy and what measures does it envisage to clarify the fate of the missing persons?
the council. unfortunately, the honourable member is quite right that democracy, human rights and the rule of law are not being respected in an acceptable way in belarus. the council is keenly aware of the situation which has existed for some time in that country and is following developments very closely. the eu has repeatedly appealed to the belarusian authorities to respect international standards in these crucial areas. at the same time, the union has taken every opportunity to promote the development of a healthy civil society in belarus. the swedish presidency will continue with great determination the efforts of the previous presidency to promote an improvement of democracy in belarus. the council considers that only through such improvement can the belarusian people fully exercise their power over the future of the country. by electing a new president this year, the people will have the opportunity to make a decisive decision about their future. within the framework of the present situation, the council will offer all possible encouragement to the democratic forces to ensure that the electorate receives a genuine and credible selection of candidates. the eu's support for civil society, individual organisations and the media is an important element in promoting democracy. as a neighbour of latvia, lithuania and poland, belarus will soon be bordering an enlarged eu. the council is therefore particularly concerned about belarus's development as a long-term partner and about ensuring stability in the region as a whole. the council is of course fully confident that the new democracies in the candidate countries will be able to cope with the challenges they may face. the three countries mentioned have all played an important and active role through their bilateral diplomatic relations with belarus. in addition, they can serve as valuable role models for belarus in terms of success in reform and democracy. like these countries, the eu has maintained that a policy of isolating belarus would be counterproductive to its own aims. the eu has therefore sought to keep the lines of communication open with the belarusian authorities and to offer them incentives for better relations. at the same time, the union continued to press for the country to fulfil its commitments and to allow the osce assistance and monitoring group freedom of action when it fully legally attempts to fulfil its mandate. in the coming weeks, the union will once again make its position known directly to the authorities in minsk. the union will of course also take this opportunity to address the case of recently disappeared persons.
i think it is quite right, as sacrédeus does, to look at developments in belarus alongside developments in russia and developments in ukraine. the work programme which the presidency will present on eu-russia cooperation to the general affairs council on monday next week speaks a lot about the need to talk to russia about the situation in the neighbouring countries of belarus and ukraine. we hope that we will also see a slightly increased understanding on the russian side of russia's responsibility to be able to have a positive impact on developments in belarus. this will then be coupled with the persistent efforts i described earlier in my opening answer. we believe it is important to influence belarus, which is closer to the rest of europe than many people might think, if they have not looked at the map properly. it is of the utmost importance that we use all the opportunities available to us from the union to bring about democratic development in belarus.
- question no 8 by mrs maría izquierdo rojo (h-0974/00) subject: persecuted women without protection or shelter in some countries women are subjected to cruel persecution and punishment, violations of the fundamental rights of the human person for which they may pay with mutilation and even with their lives. such ill-treatment is often due to the enforcement of fundamentalist laws or the enforcement of ancestral practices and traditions. the european union says it is willing to defend women against such intolerable persecution and punishment, but has not yet been able to translate its declarations into political measures and decisions that leave room for hope. would the council therefore support measures to ensure that women who are victims of such situations can be granted political asylum and refuge within the european union?
the council. the council bodies are very aware of the kind of persecution and mutilation mentioned by the honourable member in his question. the situation in the countries of origin of asylum seekers is continuously monitored by cirea, the centre for information, discussion and exchange on asylum matters. the factors mentioned here are taken into account when member states process asylum applications from victims of such abuses. however, it should be recalled that the experience of the studies carried out by cirea shows that women who have been victims of violence, rape or mutilation do not always state these reasons as the main reason for their application for asylum. as the honourable member will recall, the tampere council agreed in 1999 to work towards establishing a common european asylum system, based on the full and absolute application of the geneva convention, so as to ensure that no one is sent back to face persecution, and that this system should include approximation of the rules on recognition and the meaning of refugee status. the council also agreed that this system should be complemented by measures for other forms of protection offering an appropriate status to those in need of such protection. in december last year, the council agreed on a number of conclusions on the reception of asylum seekers. these conclusions, which will form the basis of the proposal for a council directive which the commission will present in the spring, include provisions requiring the host member state to provide specialist medical care to asylum seekers who have been subjected to torture, rape or other serious ill-treatment. the council is now awaiting the commission's proposal, and when it does come, the swedish presidency intends to deal with it as a matter of priority. the commission has also indicated its intention to present a proposal later this year on the rules for the recognition and content of refugee status and complementary forms of protection. the question of how gender-based persecution should be viewed in this context in the union will certainly be the subject of a thorough analysis.
- i would like to ask the president-in-office of the council whether he is in favour of women being treated in the european union as individuals, without having to depend on a husband or a guardian, for the purposes of visas and asylum applications. do you agree, mr president-in-office, that we should treat women who apply for visas or asylum as persons? answer me, please. i hope your answer is yes.
of course i am in favour of such an arrangement. of course, each individual should be treated as an individual. then we must also remember that in many asylum cases we are talking about family reunification of various kinds. this may mean that if one member of a family has been granted asylum, it affects the trial of other members of the same family. that is a bit of a departure from the principle of individual treatment, but the basic answer to the honourable member's question is: yes.
- question no 9 by mr niall andrews, substitute for mr crowley (h-0976/00) subject: iraq and the lifting of sanctions can the council, under the swedish presidency, indicate the degree of priority it gives to the situation in iraq and, more particularly, can it make a clear commitment to work towards the lifting of sanctions which are damaging to the health and wellbeing of men, women and children?
the council. the living conditions of the iraqi people, together with the pursuit of lasting security and stability in the region, are the main issues for the council in its policy towards iraq. the council is currently examining the possibilities for action by the union in the humanitarian and cultural fields within the framework of existing un security council resolutions on iraq. this is particularly true of the resolution on the oil for food programme. but it is also important that the iraqi government cooperate in order to implement such a programme. the european union will of course continue to fully implement the un security council resolutions against iraq. resolution 1284 of 1999 provides for the possibility of lifting sanctions, provided that the government of iraq cooperates fully with the un inspectors responsible for disarmament in iraq. in this context, the council also notes and welcomes the establishment of a un working group to draw up general recommendations on how un sanctions can be improved, how they can be better targeted and how unnecessary human suffering can be avoided.

- question no 13 by mr pat the cope gallagher (h-0985/00) subject: fisheries and the swedish presidency could the council, in the context of the swedish presidency, indicate how much importance it attaches to the fisheries sector, in view of the extremely difficult situation facing fishermen in ireland and other countries of the european union, and what are its priorities for the next development programme for the fishing fleet for the period 2002-2006 ?
the council. it is not quite clear from the honourable member's question whether it is addressed to the council or to the swedish presidency. i am glad, however, to be able to take this opportunity to state very briefly, as the honourable member would like, some priorities for the future policy of the community's fishing fleet. let me say first of all that the presidency attaches great importance to the common fisheries policy and is fully aware of the difficult situation facing the fishing industry following the drastic cuts in quotas, etc. at the council meeting last december. however, the cuts were necessary in view of the situation of fish stocks, in particular cod and hake, and also affected a number of other species. the council sees the obvious long-term remedy to this situation as establishing a lasting balance between fishing capacity and available resources to enable the sustainable exploitation of living marine resources and to ensure the future livelihoods of fishermen. the presidency therefore intends to hold a general debate in the council on the follow-up to the multiannual development programmes after the end of the fourth multiannual development programme on 31 december 2001. the commission will present its proposals shortly. we are fully aware that the current programmes have not struck a balance and that they have been controversial in some quarters. in addition to the structural problems specifically mentioned in the question, the presidency's priorities also include the launch of the commission's green paper on the future of the cfp and the preparation of a presidency proposal on fisheries and the environment, i.e. the integration of environmental issues and the principle of sustainable development into the cfp. this is part of the cardiff process and the council is obliged to present such a document to the european council in gothenburg. the presidency does not consider that there is more scope for support measures to be taken in favour of an individual member state, but rather that the cfp should be developed to the benefit of the fisheries sector throughout the union. the honourable member will have noticed that the drastic reductions in fishing opportunities will be accompanied by plans to restore the threatened stocks. in this context, we have asked the european parliament to cooperate by delivering its opinion in january on the proposal for a rescue plan for cod in the irish sea and that these measures may apply as from 14 february 2001. we appreciate the efforts made by the european parliament in this respect but are not yet convinced that this will actually become a reality. i therefore hope that parliament is prepared to cooperate with the council on this point.
i fully share the honourable member's view. when discussing these types of important issues, it is important that all concerned are properly involved in the discussion. i think it is quite obvious that such a discussion should be based on scientific evidence, but of course all those concerned, including the representatives of the fishing industry, should be able to take part in it. i can therefore assure you that we, the presidency, will do everything possible to ensure that there is a full discussion with as many people as possible on these important issues.
the question raised by the honourable member is of course very important, not least for the fishermen concerned. but i am afraid that the question has been put to the wrong person, namely the president of the council. this is, in our view, a question which should be put to the commission, which is responsible for this area, in the first instance.

the commission. mr president, i would first like to thank all members of this house, and in particular the rapporteur, mr esko seppänen, for his excellent report. the commission welcomes the report and intangible. we agree with you in particular that intangible assets such as skills, innovation and research and development are the cornerstones of the competitiveness of european industry. the main priorities are to ensure a high level of professional competence. i would like to begin by saying a few words about the importance of this industry. it accounts for 10% of the eu's total industrial output, both in terms of added value and the number of jobs created. it is worth remembering that as many as 12 million private forest owners supply wood to industry, and the industry is spread across the eu. industry is often located in remote areas where it helps to sustain economic activity, employment and infrastructure. the five main industrial sectors make up one of the largest industrial sectors in the european union. its output is worth over eur 300 billion, with a value added of eur 110 billion. it employs 2.5 million people directly, and many more indirectly. the commission communication on the state of competitiveness of forestry and related industries took a new look at industry as a cluster, where the performance of each sector influences the competitiveness of other sectors. in this type of group examination, the analysis of individual sectors is reduced, but the questions can be considered from a broader perspective. the communication provides a basis for continuing assessment of the factors affecting the competitiveness of the industry concerned. the commission has therefore carried out a series of sectoral studies on the forestry and related industries. the studies on the graphic and mechanical industries have already been published. in addition, the commission has set up two channels to deal with different issues, as a follow-up to the present communication. the first is the advisory committee on forestry and forest-based industries, which was relaunched in 1997, and the second is the forum on forestry and related industries. the forum has a key role in enabling systematic analysis of key issues and effective interaction with businesses, industry organisations and other stakeholders. the forum also brings together representatives of community institutions, such as the european parliament and the commission, and of the member states. the first forum was held here in strasbourg at the beginning of september at the level of the authorities, and i can say that the rapporteur, mr seppänen, also took part in this forum. it also discussed issues relating to publishing, which mr flesch mentioned: it dealt with electronic commerce and intellectual property rights. the next forum will be held in stockholm in june. it will further explore how forest-based and related industries can contribute to sustainable development and optimise their contribution to environmental protection at all stages of the wood chain, from forest to end products. sustainability is becoming increasingly important. the european council in gothenburg in june will take important decisions in this area. forest-based industries are those sectors in which all the economic, social and environmental components of sustainable development are closely interdependent. the forest-based industry uses renewable raw materials and state-of-the-art recycling and energy recovery methods, and can therefore make a particularly significant contribution to sustainable development. i would reply to mr flesch's question as follows: we are well aware that the spending sector is different from the actual forestry industry today, it includes paper-based production as well as many other things. the problem in the commission has been that the resources of the enterprise dg have been reduced by 20% over the last or in which sectoral context the spending area would be best placed. i will be in touch with industry representatives after this discussion. i would like to thank mr seppänen once again for his excellent report and the other members for their contribution to this work. coherence of our actions. not everyone understands that we must set the priority of enlargement to the east against the priority of the mediterranean. i believe, moreover, that the president-in-office of the council, mrs lindh, made this clear in committee the other day. these are two genuine but different priorities. enlargement is an operational priority, where we have set objectives, we know where we are going, we know what we want and, in fact, there are no alternative strategic options. the mediterranean policy is a strategic priority, where we do not know where we are going, or, to be more precise, we are inexorably going where we do not want to go. the foreseeable development of incomes, taking into account the current demographics and economic growth, indicates that our average per capita income will rise and the average per capita income in north africa will fall and, if there is no change in this, the problems that we all have in mind will increase, and which i do not think it is necessary to mention. we know what will happen, but we don't know how to prevent it, even if we want to avoid it at all costs. so let us not oppose political priorities. my other reflection is on the consistency of our actions. because to get results, we have to be more consistent. it is clear that the will is lacking and the resources are lacking, but it turns out that the resources are not being used, and this means that there is not enough management capacity on our part and not enough absorption capacity on the part of the recipient countries. you ask for more and you don't consume. so someone may ask, 'why don't we just adjust the figures?' but the truth is that the budget is needed, and it must be used. i think that this requires conviction and absorption. i hope that these reports will help to find the right method, but i am not convinced of that, to be honest.
mr president, i shall concentrate on one aspect of the common strategy for the mediterranean region which is not being taken into account in its entirety: the south-south dialogue, which is an important motor within the strategy for the relationship between the european union and the maghreb countries. the creation of centralised bodies and mechanisms that look into the most pressing problems is imperative. the management of projects on specific points and on common aspects is a necessity which has become a reality in cases where, in a private capacity, citizens and cities on both sides of the strait of gibraltar have been collaborating with magnificent results and without community auspices. for this local management, it would be necessary to create a new body which, as a decentralised and permanent mechanism, would bring together the institutional, political and social leaders of these territories, which are so close and so far apart at the same time. the 14 kilometres that separate the european union from the maghreb are real, but let us not allow them to become an insurmountable distance that prevents closer cooperation. immigration, its causes and consequences - sometimes terrible and irreparable - business, agricultural and fisheries exchanges, social, technical, training and university exchanges, aspects of common development, such as in the energy sector, and the fundamental democratizing political aspects which the european union must promote in these countries call for the creation of new mechanisms and instruments which, in a decentralised way, respond to these local needs but which have a general impact.

problems of the southern mediterranean - political upheaval, economic stagnation, population growth - affect us, directly or indirectly, as europeans. the same applies to the flows of migrants we mr president, the idea that the mediterranean is the number one priority of the european union's foreign policy stems from the conviction that the mediterranean - which is no longer the centre of the world - is, in any case, the focal point of all the major contradictions and challenges of the 21st century. the issue of war and peace is particularly present in the mediterranean. the subject of north-south relations is spectacularly alive in the mediterranean. the mediterranean is a very fashionable theme of clash of civilizations or dialogue of cultures. the emergence of xenophobia and racism, or of tolerance and miscegenation, has its climax in the mediterranean. the question of democracy and human rights or authoritarianism is alive in the mediterranean and will continue to be for years to come. the issue of the regional response to the challenges of globalisation is raised in the mediterranean. the issue of women's emancipation or submission is also most prominent in the mediterranean region. we must not insist that this is our main priority, because future scenarios are completely open to it, whereas enlargement will have its course, its costs, its incidents, but no one can reasonably imagine any other scenario than that of its completion. in the mediterranean, you can get a sandbelt or a slumbelt in the 21st century, and both issues are dramatically raised. the two contributions which are being presented here today in the european parliament are contributions to the relaunch of the euro-mediterranean policy. i think that mr patten and mr solana would do well to read these reports to each other and, in particular, the report by my friend and teacher, sami naïr, because it is a very coherent, very well-crafted list, which inspires a political proposal. this is a policy which was well defined in barcelona five years ago, but which today requires not only a renewed will but also concrete initiatives. we must achieve - especially in the mediterranean, we know that - something very important: the explanation of things. however, if there is a lack today, it is the lack of a concrete symbol, of a strong signal that the union, the council, the commission and parliament are really interested in this relaunch beyond words and narratives. in this connection, i would like to draw attention to an aspect of the sami naïr report: the need to develop strong initiatives in the field of south-south trade and subregional integration or integration in the southern mediterranean. we need something strong, i do not know exactly what it can be, but something which can really captivate public opinion in the south so that they see that the european union, beyond a well-planned policy, clearly has the will to create banking and financial instruments, railways which integrate the south subregionally or motorway or highway networks. and a message which really contributes to this renewed will to integrate, which, especially in the maghreb, is being raised with hope at the moment and which must count on an ambitious and also generous contribution from the union.
we are familiar with the catalogue of problems and their causes affecting the euro-mediterranean area, mr president, mr commissioner: they are basically the same as in 1995, when the barcelona process was launched. the debate has already mentioned: illegal immigration, droughts, the external debt, the lack of respect for human rights and terrorism, which mercilessly destroys the lives of innocent people and families, as we are suffering in spain, algeria and the middle east itself. today, more than ever, we must proclaim that only cooperation, dialogue, economic and cultural exchanges, solidarity and mutual understanding can make the two shores of the mediterranean a prosperous and peaceful area. neither the european union nor the maghreb and mashreq countries can afford to waste the human and cultural resources which enrich the region. the problem is we're not hitting that line. the association agreements are dead letters in many respects. the financial instruments are not being used as they should be and the political, economic and social development of these countries is not keeping pace with the pace of much-needed horizontal cooperation or with the modernity demanded by a world that is advancing at a rapid pace in terms of technology. it is time to move from the muses to the theatre, to demand efficiency and effectiveness from the efforts of the strategy that has been designed and, in that sense, i would like to emphasize the request for reinforcement of human resources that has been made by our colleague gerardo galeote.
mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteurs, mrs muscardini and mr naïr, on the excellent work they have done on a sensitive issue in this part of the world. i would also like to begin this speech by informing this parliament - which i believe is good news - about the meda programme, which some of you may already know. on 12 december the council adopted a budgetary allocation for this purpose, representing an increase of 10% over the annual investment of the meda programme. this means that the annual allocation will now be eur 764 million per year, compared with eur 684 million in the previous period. i think this shows the good spirit which has governed relations between parliament, the commission and the council in this area. but on the other hand - and unfortunately - we must note that not enough resources are being put to ensure that this aid is properly allocated, since in the period 1995-1999 almost 30% of the budgeted assistance was not implemented. it's a disappointing run. i don't know what's wrong, but something's wrong. on the other hand, i would also like to mention the social, cultural and human dimension of these 15 north african countries, to which we must bring our different societies closer, promote understanding and improve mutual understanding. the education and training of the young also requires special effort, and must be based on tolerance, since they are the future of these nations. we cannot forget dialogue and the promotion of fundamental rights. finally, i would like to say one thing: we are obliged to do it well, because if we do not do it out of love, we must do it out of fear, because the safeguarding of southern europe is at stake.
the council. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your report. the middle east peace process is in a precarious state in view of the israeli election of a prime minister on 6 february. the negotiations in taba brought the parties closer to a negotiated solution than they had ever been. at the same time, the violence in the palestinian territories and the high number of dead and wounded have seriously reduced the level of trust between the negotiating parties. the israeli government is facing change, regardless of the outcome of the february 6th prime ministers' elections, but the will for peace should hopefully be strong in both the israeli and palestinian public at the same time. the election of the prime minister of israel and the formation of the next government will be important factors in determining the future direction of the peace process. despite the difficulties, the parties did not want to lose the progress achieved. in taba, the parties negotiated directly with each other and without any third party being present. the atmosphere was serious and result-oriented, and both sides expressed optimism this time about the possibilities of reaching a final settlement. however, time did not permit such a final settlement to be reached at taba, but the parties agreed on 28 january to a joint concluding statement. this statement can provide a platform to build on the day when negotiations on a final settlement are resumed. i would draw the attention of honourable members and of parliament to the fact that this statement particularly emphasizes the role of the european union in the continuing peace process. the presidency and other addressees are being asked from many quarters to strengthen the union's already strong commitment to the whole middle east issue. the eu has an important role to play in that it is the main trading partner for virtually all the countries in the region and the largest donor of public aid to the palestinian territories. the eu, through its special representative mr moratinos, who was present throughout, was able to follow the negotiations in taba. it was of great
